segments.source: Counter Culture says Even Keel combines regular and decaffeinated organic coffees in a 50/50 blend. It is distinct from Slow Motion, the full-decaf product, and from buying two bags to mix at home. The current roast-date selector shows several historical combinations; visible text does not reliably pair each component list with the selected period, so this review does not assign one origin percentage table to a bag it has not seen. The variety and decaffeination route of the complete current blend are not established by the accessible page.

segments.source: The reason to choose this bag is routine simplicity. If distinctive flavor is the priority, a buyer may prefer to combine two coffees they already like, but that adds weighing and grinder-switch work. Even Keel trades that control for one packaged recipe.

segments.source: Counter Culture publishes a French-press start of 50 g coffee to 800 g water at 205°F with a six-minute schedule. That is a 1:16 ratio for that method, not an espresso target. The bag can be ground for another brewer, but the water and grind should follow that brewer rather than a generic half-caff rule.

segments.source: Mixing regular and decaf beans does not make the cup’s caffeine exactly one half of a particular regular coffee. Bean lots and brewing extraction vary, and we have no assay for Even Keel. If a strict caffeine limit matters, ask the roaster for product-specific information or use an independently measured option; do not infer milligrams from the 50/50 ingredient statement.

segments.source: Equator calls Eye of the Tiger a seasonally evolving espresso blend and says the component profile may change about every three months. The accessible product page checked October 16 currently names Costa Rica Tarrazú honey-processed Catuai from Hermanos Monge Ureña and washed Bourbon from Rwanda’s Nyampinga Cooperative. A separately indexed version of the same URL showed Guatemala, Colombia and Papua New Guinea. That is evidence of change or indexing lag, not two compositions to merge. Use the live record and the delivered bag for your roast date.

segments.source: Cherry cola, gingersnap and chocolate are the current roaster notes. Equator describes a light, bright espresso and says the Costa Rican coffee contributes body and sweet fruit, while the Rwandan component adds citrus and spice. These are the roaster’s descriptions, not a Coffeedant sensory finding. The Kitchn tasted an older Eye of the Tiger bag in a home espresso context; its favorable impression cannot confirm today’s components or our cup.

segments.source: Equator’s current espresso panel uses 18 g coffee and 46 g beverage, labeled 1:2.5, with a 23-second example on a Barista Express. The masses are an actionable start if your basket accepts 18 g. The time and grind are not promises on another machine. A scale and fresh whole beans allow you to compare the actual shot with the roaster’s target.
